intent: Make the 500-line file-length test see the repo's real Python sources. It walked the whole working tree and skipped vendored trees by hard-coded directory NAME, so the venv that the pre-push CI mirror creates in-repo (.ci-mirror-venv, not the listed .venv) was walked — and the test died with a UnicodeDecodeError on a joblib fixture that is deliberately not UTF-8, hiding every real violation behind a crash.
scope: python_pkg/tests/test_file_length.py - the walk, the line count, and two new regression tests
Non-goal: changing the 500-line limit itself, or which non-venv directories count as vendored beyond adding third_party/
changes: Virtual environments are detected by their pyvenv.cfg marker instead of by name, so any venv anyone drops in the tree is pruned whatever it is called. Naming them one at a time is precisely what failed here.
The walk uses os.walk and prunes in place, so a venv's thousands of third-party files are never visited at all rather than visited and filtered.
Lines are counted from bytes (read_bytes().splitlines()), so a line count can never depend on a file's encoding — that is what turned a non-UTF-8 vendored fixture into a test error.

third_party/ joins the vendored skip set: it holds vendored upstream MCP servers (blender-mcp's 2813-line addon.py, wander-agent's 1835-line server.py, ...) which the repo's own 500-line rule does not govern.
Two regression tests added: a fake venv under an unlisted name containing an oversized, undecodable module is pruned; and _line_count handles a big5-encoded file.

verification.evidence: 3 passed. Before the fix: UnicodeDecodeError on .ci-mirror-venv/.../test_func_inspect_special_encoding.py. Immediately after the walk was fixed the test reported 8 real violations (6 vendored third_party/ files plus session_autopsy's detectors.py 559 and parse.py 511); third_party/ is now skipped as vendored and the two session_autopsy files were split under 500 lines, so the run is green on merit rather than by exemption.

verification.command: python -m pytest python_pkg -q (full suite with coverage gate)
verification.evidence: 876 passed; TOTAL coverage 100% (3874 statements, 1124 branches), fail_under=100 satisfied. Test files are coverage-omitted, so the new helpers add no coverage debt.

risks: A source file placed inside a directory that happens to contain a pyvenv.cfg is no longer checked. That is the intended trade: such a directory IS a virtualenv.
third_party/ is now unchecked wholesale. Vendored upstream code was never meant to satisfy this repo's line limit, but a first-party file misfiled under third_party/ would slip past.

Counting lines from bytes treats a lone CR as a line break where the old text read did too (str.splitlines and bytes.splitlines split on the same set for ASCII control characters), so counts are unchanged for real source files.
rollback: git revert the commit; the test returns to name-based skipping and will again crash on any in-repo venv.
After rollback, re-run python -m pytest python_pkg/tests/test_file_length.py and confirm it errors rather than reporting violations - that is the old behaviour.
